reviews.suggested_text: At that time Raphael, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said to me, “These hollow places[a] are for the spirits of the souls of the dead[b] to be gathered into them. For this purpose they were created: to gather here all the souls of the children of men.”

reviews.reason: Three must remain: Greek note 6 proposes four, but that is not the selected reading. The English omits the opening answer-and-speech formula and makes the righteous spirits the subject despite the supplied preposition discussed in note 28: the clause describes a place set apart for them. The printed separation verb reads ይትፈለጥ, not the candidate's ይትፈለጠ. Bright spring remains unapproved: note 32 emends ብርሃን to ብርህት with Greek φωτεινή, following Flemming. Merely retaining above it does not establish the antecedent of በላዕሌሁ or the adjective's Ethiopic attachment. Next evidence: a grammatical analysis of the complete relative clause, including noun gender and the singular suffix, distinguishing the printed Ethiopic from the Greek-assisted reconstruction.

reviews.reason: Both negatives are preserved across the page boundary, but English they naturally refers back to souls and obscures the grammatical change. The killing verb is feminine singular with the soul expression; the rising verb is masculine plural, referring to the people. The small raised apparatus numbers after the continuation are note calls, not apostrophes belonging to the Geʿez wording. Verse 13 ends before the separately numbered blessing.
reviews.suggested_text: And likewise a place was made for the souls of people who were not righteous but sinners, complete in transgression, and who will be with the transgressors, like them.[a] But their souls will not be killed on the day of judgment, and those people will not rise from here.[b]
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain [a]. Replace [b]: “The first negative governs the feminine-singular soul expression; the second governs a masculine-plural verb referring to the people. Those people makes that grammatical distinction explicit. Printed page 60, notes 1–2, reports variants in the rising/from-here wording; neither negative is removed here. This is a statement about the described group, not every soul.”
